item.title: Kolbe Windows & Doors expands door hardware portfolio
item.description:
WAUSAU, Wis. — Kolbe Windows & Doors expands its portfolio of premium door hardware with the introduction of the exclusive Fort Worth Handle Sets. Designed for swinging and sliding doors, Fort Worth builds upon the success of the popular Dallas handle set with refined aesthetics, enhanced ergonomics and thoughtful functionality.

Developed through customer feedback and a meticulous design process, the Fort Worth Handle Set represents the next evolution in Kolbe door hardware. The Kolbe team focused on the details that influence everyday interactions, from how the handle feels in hand to how it complements contemporary architectural design.

“Fort Worth was designed to preserve the familiar qualities customers appreciated in the Dallas handle set, while refining key elements to improve both appearance and performance,” said Liz Reynolds, director of marketing for Kolbe Windows & Doors. “The result is a handle set that feels intuitive to operate, while contributing to a cohesive design experience throughout the home.”

Key features of the Fort Worth Handle Sets include:

  • Refined Handle Shape provides a comfortable, ergonomic grip for both right- and left-handed users.
  • Modern V-Knob Thumb Turn introduces a clean, contemporary look to the interior side of the door.
  • Integrated Key Cylinder built directly into the exterior escutcheon, eliminates protrusion and creates a streamlined appearance.
  • Hidden Fasteners enhance aesthetics, while supporting durability and easier maintenance.
  • Consistent Design Across Swinging and Sliding Doors coordinates the desired look throughout a project.

Available exclusively from Kolbe, Fort Worth Handle Sets are offered for compatible swinging and sliding doors in the VistaLuxe WD LINE, Ultra Series and Heritage Series. Multiple finish options are available, including Matte Black, Satin Nickel, White, Rustic Umber and Unlacquered Brass, along with select mixed-finish combinations that allow designers and homeowners additional creative flexibility.

To learn more, visit Kolbe’s website or contact a local Kolbe dealer.

item.title: MasterBrand announces CFO transition
item.description:
BEACHWOOD, Ohio — MasterBrand, Inc., the largest residential cabinet manufacturer in North America, has appointed Mark Young vice president and interim chief financial officer, effective immediately. He succeeds Andrea Simon, who has agreed to remain with the company in an advisory capacity through March 31, 2027, to facilitate a seamless transition. The company has initiated a comprehensive search process, with the assistance of a leading executive search firm, to identify a permanent CFO from internal and external candidates. Simon’s departure is not related to any issues with respect to the integrity of the Company’s financial statements or accounting policies and practices.

“On behalf of the Board and management team, I'd like to thank Andi for her many contributions to MasterBrand over the past six years,” said Dave Banyard, MasterBrand’s president and chief executive officer. “Her leadership helped establish MasterBrand as a standalone public company, and now is the right time to make this transition. We wish her all the best.”

Young has served as MasterBrand’s VP and chief accounting officer since joining the Company in 2022. In this role he has been responsible for financial reporting, internal controls, and accounting policy. He has more than 20 years of finance and accounting leadership experience across the manufacturing industry and public accounting. Prior to joining MasterBrand, Young held accounting leadership roles at Cooper Tire & Rubber Company, where he led the global accounting function and SEC reporting.

Banyard continued, “Mark’s deep knowledge of our strategic priorities and financial operations makes him well positioned to serve as interim CFO at this important point in our integration journey following the merger with American Woodmark. Mark’s understanding of both businesses and prior integration experience will be instrumental in advancing the work underway. The Board and I have full confidence in his ability to lead the finance organization while we conduct a search for a permanent CFO.”

item.title: Pittsburgh Paints Company releases Veloura Trim, Door, and Cabinet finish
item.description:
CRANBERRY TWP., Pa. — The Pittsburgh Paints brand has launched Pittsburgh Paints Veloura Trim, Door and Cabinet Interior and Exterior Waterborne Urethane Alkyd Enamel. With Smoothflow technology, Veloura enamel delivers exceptional flow and leveling, best-in-class hide and coverage, and a smooth, factory-like finish for trim, doors and cabinets.

“We heard that our customers wanted a premium interior and exterior urethane product that delivered exceptional application characteristics and finish quality,” said Dennis Karnstein, president of Commercial, Pittsburgh Paints Co. “Our teams came together to develop a product designed to not only meet but exceed those expectations.”

The Veloura enamel’s durable formula withstands repeated cleaning and offers excellent block resistance and hardness for lasting performance. With a low odor and low volatile organic compound (VOC) formula, Veloura enamel delivers enduring beauty with effortless application, combining durability, elegance and sustainability in each coat.

As the latest addition to the Pittsburgh Paints product portfolio, Veloura enamel delivers the following performance features:

  • Smoothflow technology with exceptional flow and leveling for unparalleled, effortless application compared to leading urethane enamels].
  • Best-in-class hide and coverage, requiring less material.
  • Smooth finished appearance for a great look across application methods.
  • Excellent block resistance and hardness, providing a tack-free, durable film.
  • Durability built to withstand repeated cleaning, resistant to gloss change and color loss from scrubbing.
  • Low VOC (<50G/L) compliant in all regulated areas.

"This launch strengthens our Pittsburgh Paints portfolio and is another example of how quickly we can respond to market needs with solutions that help our customers succeed,” said Karnstein. “This product competes with leading urethane enamels in the market to provide the durability professionals and homeowners expect.”

To celebrate, Pittsburgh Paints will host Veloura Day on November 5 at approximately 50 Pittsburgh Paints store locations nationwide. Representatives will hold live demos of Veloura enamel and other products from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. local time.

Veloura enamel is recommended for trim, doors,cabinets, shelving and more and is available in satin and semi-gloss sheens at Pittsburgh Paints stores nationwide, select Pittsburgh Paints dealers, and online at ppgpaints.com/veloura/veloura.

The Pittsburgh Paints brand is part of The Pittsburgh Paints Company, a leading producer of interior and exterior paints, stains, caulks, repair products, adhesives and sealants for homeowners and professionals in the United States.

item.title: Bill introduced to expand domestic mass timber production
item.description:
PORTLAND — A bipartisan bill has been introduced to the House of Representatives: the Mass Timber Growth and Innovation Act looks to lower housing construction costs, strengthen American manufacturing, and create good-paying jobs in rural communities. The bill would provide tax incentives to expand domestic production of mass timber, an innovative wood building material that can help builders construct homes faster and at a lower cost.

“Every Oregon family deserves a home they can afford. Right now, Oregon needs to build nearly 500,000 new homes over the next 20 years to keep up with demand, but we simply aren’t building enough, and the restricted supply leads to increased prices,” said U.S. Congresswoman Andrea Salinas. “Mass timber can help us build faster and more affordably. Oregon has led the wood products industry for generations, and this bill provides the opportunity for Oregon workers lead what comes next. That means more homes for working families and more good jobs in the rural towns that helped build this state. I look forward to working with Rep. Thompson to get this done.”

Manufacturers face significant barriers to expanding production of mass timber. Building new facilities and purchasing specialized equipment require substantial upfront investments. Limited domestic manufacturing capacity has contributed to higher material prices, making it harder for builders to adopt mass timber construction.
The Mass Timber Growth and Innovation Act would:

  1. Help manufacturers build new plants. The bill offers a 10 percent tax credit for investments in mass timber manufacturing facilities, including machinery, equipment, and buildings. It does this by adding mass timber to the existing Advanced Manufacturing Investment Credit.
  2. Reward research that brings costs down. This bill creates a 20 percent credit that covers every dollar a company spends on mass timber research, from new products to better production methods.

For Oregon, expanding mass timber manufacturing presents an opportunity to build on the state's timber and wood products industry while supporting economic growth in rural communities. Increased production could create new demand for American-grown wood, support family-wage manufacturing jobs, and help builders access more affordable construction materials.

The bill is endorsed by: American Wood Council, Chamber of Progress, Oregon Forest Industries Council, Washington Mass Timber Accelerator, and Weyerhaeuser.

The full text of the bill is available here.

item.title: Wood Pro Expo Lancaster closes after two days of industry exchange
item.description:
MANHEIM, Pa. — Wood Pro Expo Lancaster concluded its two-day run at Spooky Nook Sports Center on Oct. 23, bringing woodworking professionals together with equipment suppliers, materials providers and industry experts for a focused look at ways to improve their businesses.

The expo floor featured solutions spanning industrial woodworking machinery, dust collection, finishing products, abrasives, software, hardware and materials. Exhibitors offered attendees a chance to explore equipment and products firsthand, ask questions and discuss how different solutions could fit into their operations.

The measure of a successful show is not simply the size of its exhibit hall. It is also what people take away from it, whether that means identifying a potential investment, finding a new source for materials, developing a sales lead or returning to work with a fresh perspective on a familiar challenge.

As Wood Pro Expo closes for another year, those practical takeaways remain central to this trade show's role in the regional woodworking industry.

Next stop, Texas and New Jersey

In 2027, Wood Pro Expo will head to Dallas, Texas for the dual Wood Pro Expo & Closets Conference show and Wood Pro Expo Northeast, held in Edison, New Jersey.

For more information about Wood Pro Expo Texas & Closets Conference, visit this link.

Stay tuned for more information about Wood Pro Expo Northeast.

item.title: Executive order supports affordable housing
item.description:
President Donald Trump signed the "Decreasing Housing Costs for the American People" executive order on October 22, 2026. The directive aims to lower housing costs, which comes ahead of the midterm elections, where inflation and affordability have been some of voters' main concerns.

“Homeownership is a vital pillar of our great Nation, and President Trump and his Administration are working tirelessly to cut burdensome costs and red tape to make the American dream of homeownership more affordable for all Americans,” the White House said in a statement.

The Executive order was me with enthusiasm by some industry groups. The National Association of Home Builders, for example, lauded the move.

“NAHB commends President Trump and his administration for making housing a national priority," said Bill Owens, chairman of the NAHB and a home builder and remodeler from Worthington, Ohio. "The president’s executive order will help reduce single-family housing and mortgage costs. We urge the administration to continue its efforts to reduce regulatory burdens to make housing more affordable for all Americans.”

Shannon McGahn, executive vice president and chief advocacy officer of the National Association of REALTORS, issued the following statement after President Trump announced a new Executive Order on housing affordability:

“The National Association of REALTORS applauds the Administration’s continued efforts to make housing more affordable and expand access to the American dream of homeownership. President Trump’s latest Executive Order helps address the costs associated with homeownership and takes steps toward making homeownership more sustainable for American families. We appreciate the President’s continued focus on this critical issue and look forward to reviewing the Administration’s proposals in greater detail. We also look forward to working with federal policymakers to advance practical solutions that lower costs, expand housing opportunities, and help more Americans achieve the dream of homeownership.”

According to a White House fact sheet, the executive order requires the Federal Housing Finance Agency to create a pilot program proactively canceling mortgage insurance for eligible borrowers with government-backed home loans. The order also directs FHFA to expand an existing program allowing borrowers to qualify for government-sponsored mortgages by using less expensive alternatives to title insurance.

The document calls on the departments of Veterans Affairs and Agriculture to reduce the interest rates on the single-family mortgages offered by their housing programs.

The order also establishes a multiagency task force to support innovation in manufactured-home development, which the administration and Congress have promoted as a potential solution to rising housing construction costs.

item.title: Unilin launches 'world’s first MDF' with up to 25% recycled wood fibers
item.description:
Unilin, a supplier of interior and construction products and part of Mohawk Group, says that it has become the first manufacturer worldwide to launch MDF panels containing up to 25% recycled fibers.

The launch marks the latest milestone in a journey that started in 2021, when Unilin developed the Osiris, a technology to recycle MDF and HDF fibers at industrial scale. Following years of testing and a €20 million investment to scale up the technology, the company has now translated its pioneering MDF and HDF recycling technology into a commercial product.

The launch follows the commissioning of the new recycling plant in Bazeilles, northern France. The plant has an annual capacity of 70,000 metric tonnes of recycled wood fibers and is estimated to postpone 130,000 metric tonnes of CO₂ emissions per year. 

From waste to raw material
Until recently, discarded MDF and HDF panels ended up in incinerators or landfills. Unlike particleboard, MDF and HDF have historically been extremely difficult to recycle because you couldn't recover wood fibers at a quality high enough to make new panels. Thanks to Unilin’s patented Osiris technology, wood fibers can now be given a second life. This keeps CO₂ stored in the wood for longer and gives valuable raw materials a new purpose.

“What seemed impossible for years is now a reality,” says Geert Coudenys, R&D Director at Unilin Panels. “By processing used MDF and HDF again, we significantly extend the life cycle of wood fibers. This gives new trees the opportunity to grow and store CO₂, while reducing our dependence on virgin raw materials. It is a technology that delivers environmental benefits without compromising the economics.”

With Osiris, Unilin cracked a challenge the industry had been trying to solve for decades. Unilin first announced the breakthrough in 2021 and subsequently developed an industrial pilot line at its MDF/HDF production site in Bazeilles, France. After successfully testing and refining the technology, the company invested €20 million in a full-scale industrial recycling installation.

The technology separates wood fibers without breaking them. MDF waste is first defibrated using steam and then carefully purified. This keeps the fibers intact and suitable for use in the existing MDF and HDF production process. The biggest challenge? Removing impurities while ensuring that the recovered fibers achieve the same quality as virgin fibers.

Extensive testing has since confirmed that the recycled MDF wood fibers meet the same performance standards as virgin fibers, with no compromise on mechanical strength.

“With the invention of Osiris in 2021, we achieved a world-first breakthrough,” says Julien Boucher, Plant Manager in Bazeilles. “Over the past few years, we have continued to refine the technology on an industrial pilot line, and the world’s first full-scale MDF and HDF recycling plant has now been operational for a year. It is a turning point for our site and for the industry as a whole.”

Ambitions and impact on the industry
The new installation has an annual capacity of 70,000 metric tonnes of recycled wood fibers. This postpones 130,000 metric tonnes of CO₂ emissions each year, comparable to the annual emissions of around 100,000 cars (based on the average emissions of new European cars). Thanks to Osiris, not only MDF but also the HDF core of laminate flooring, such as Quick-Step, can become circular.

The first panels containing recycled fibers are now on the market. Unilin offers these MDF panels on request with up to 25% recycled fibers, using an ISCC PLUS-certified mass balance system. And this is only the beginning. In the future, Unilin aims for recycled fibers to make up a quarter of the MDF wood fibre mix across all its sites. This broader sustainability approach also received international recognition last summer: Unilin was awarded an EcoVadis Gold medal, placing the company among the top 5% of companies assessed by EcoVadis worldwide.

Unilin is also looking beyond its own production. Unilin is making the technology available to the industry through licensing. 

Bert Vandenkendelaere, president of Unilin Panels, said, “We believe this breakthrough will help move not only our company forward, but the entire industry. The major challenge now is to establish separate wood waste streams. That requires collaboration across the entire value chain, from collectors to processors and manufacturers. Only by working together can we accelerate the transition to a circular industry.”

This project was co-funded by the French government as part of France 2030, managed by ADEME, with financial support from La Région Grand Est.

item.title: What cabinet manufacturers should expect from a door supplier
item.description:
As demand for customized cabinetry grows, manufacturers face a challenge beyond offering more styles, materials and finishes. They must also ensure the components they source meet quality expectations, arrive when needed and integrate seamlessly into finished products.

For cabinet makers and home builders, a cabinet door is more than a design element. It is a critical component in a larger production and installation schedule. Delays, incomplete orders or inconsistent quality disrupts that process, creating additional work for manufacturers and potentially affecting project timelines. That makes choosing the right cabinet door supplier critically important.

“Manufacturers need suppliers they can count on,” said Steve Bloch, Product Manager at Lexington Manufacturing. “The doors must meet quality expectations, the materials and finishes need to match, and the order needs to arrive complete and on time. All those things matter to keeping production moving.”

Reliability beyond the product
Dimensional consistency is important when sourcing cabinet doors, but manufacturers also need to understand the entire supply relationship.

An order that arrives late or incomplete creates complications well beyond the receiving dock. Production schedules and installation dates are affected, and workers waste time tracking down missing pieces or coordinating replacements. On-time, complete delivery helps manufacturers plan with greater confidence, whether fulfilling a large production run or managing a smaller custom project.

Quality is obviously important. Cabinet doors are highly visible components, and defects or variations affect the appearance of the finished cabinetry. Manufacturers need products that meet specifications at high quality, as their customers expect.

“It's not just about producing a door that looks right on its own,” Bloch said. “It needs to meet requirements and arrive in a condition that allows the manufacturer to move forward.”

Material matching matters
Material and finish matching present another critical consideration, particularly when a door incorporates multiple materials or components.

Variations in color, grain or finish detract from the appearance of a door, even when its dimensions are correct. These details become especially important when manufacturers are coordinating cabinet doors with drawer fronts or other elements in a larger cabinetry system.

Evaluating a supplier's approach to material selection, finish consistency and quality control helps manufacturers determine whether a door program will meet their needs.

Five-piece doors offer design flexibility
Five-piece cabinet doors remain a versatile option for manufacturers serving a range of customer preferences. Their construction accommodates different profiles, materials and finishes, supporting traditional and contemporary designs within a familiar format.

In April 2026, Lexington Manufacturing expanded beyond cabinet components with the launch of its Cabinet Door Program, introducing full five-piece cabinet doors for manufacturers and distributors. The program gives manufacturers another sourcing option as they balance design flexibility with production requirements.

“Manufacturers want options, but they also need a dependable process for getting those products into production,” Bloch said. “A production-ready door program simplifies sourcing while giving manufacturers flexibility in the projects they take on.”

Evaluating a supplier
When assessing cabinet door suppliers, manufacturers should consider several factors beyond style availability. Customization creates opportunities for cabinet manufacturers to differentiate their products. Realizing those opportunities, however, requires dependable partners who understand that a successful order involves more than the door itself.

Reliable delivery, quality construction and careful material matching turn product choices into finished cabinetry they can confidently deliver to their customers.

item.title: Ethan Allen releasing results after annual meeting, drawing ire from investor
item.description:
DANBURY, Ct. — Ethan Allen Interiors Inc. announced it will release its financial and operational results for the fiscal 2027 first quarter ended September 30, 2026, after the stock market closes on Monday, November 9, 2026.

Following the release, the Company will host a conference call at 5:00 p.m. (ET) to discuss these results.

The date for releasing its fiscal first quarter results will come days after Ethan Allen's November 4 Annual Meeting, where shareholders will decide who oversees the Company’s future.

Doug Bergeron, the leader of the investor group looking to wrest management control of the company, issued a press release calling on Ethan Allen to set its earnings date immediately and release first quarter results before shareholders vote. 

“For more than 20 years, Ethan Allen has reported its first quarter results ahead of its annual meeting," said Bergeron. "The Board adhered to that schedule even during its 2015 proxy contest. Further, for the past five years, the Company has consistently released its first quarter results on the last Wednesday of October – a schedule that has been seemingly automatic. The Board’s decision to abandon these practices now is all the more concerning and appears to be a deliberate attempt to manipulate the information available to shareholders as they cast their votes."

item.title: Video: Massive fire destroys Pennsylvania millwork company
item.description:
BLAIR COUNTY, Pa. — More than 100 first responders from over two dozen emergency and fire crews from three counties battled a massive blaze at Cove Mountain Wood Products in Roaring Spring, Pennsylvania. 

No one was injured in the Oct. 21 fire, but more than an estimated $1 million worth of products and the structure were destroyed in the fire, according to an early report by Friendship Fire Company Chief James Musselman.

Firefighters, who fought the fire for roughly five hours, had to shuttle water tankers from a nearby pond due to local water supply challenges.

While the official cause remains under investigation, emergency officials believe it may be accidental and linked to finishing materials stored inside the building.

"Unfortunately, due to the amount of flammable materials and fuel load that were in the building due to its use as a woodworking business, it’s unknown what the initial cause of the fire was and is being ruled accidental/undetermined, according to the Friendship Fire Company's Facebook page. The property was self-insured by the owner. 

The Friendship Fire Company was dispatched at 7:03 p.m. after a Martinsburg police car passing by the building noticed smoke.

Upon arrival, Musselman told the Altoona Mirror that he saw fire emerging through the back right section of the roof and spreading to the other side of the building.

"They have a lot of stains and chemicals, so there's a lot of flammable stuff," he said.

The company's website describes the company as a one-stop millwork destination for hardwood flooring, trimwork, finishing pieces, and other milling products.

According to the fire department's report, the owner of the property requested for machinery to bring down the rest of the building and assist with clearing the debris. Two excavators and skid steers were brought in to clear the debris as crews worked to finish extinguishing hot spots.
